Daniel Kinahan, a suspected leader of a major criminal organization, was extradited from the UAE to Dublin to face charges of directing a criminal group. He is currently remanded in custody until October.

International police cooperation has successfully bridged a jurisdictional gap that previously allowed high-level suspects to operate with relative impunity.

This is a WHO/WHERE error. The focus is on the individual (Kinahan) rather than the systemic conditions that allowed the cartel to thrive globally for decades.

By aligning police forces across borders, the state moved from reactive posturing to active integration. This reduces the strain of jurisdictional friction, though it does not yet solve the underlying market demand for illicit goods.
